policy: iteration-2/grading-policy.md; binary Juice Shop root-cause scoring; report evidence only; source-only adjudication

expectations.text: SQL injection in login (string-built query)
expectations.evidence: WSA-001 (report.md:24–30) identifies routes/login.ts:33: email is concatenated into SQL and a selected row becomes an authenticated session; correctly retains the MFA prerequisite.

expectations.text: SQL injection in product search
expectations.evidence: WSA-001 (report.md:24–30) names routes/search.ts:20–22 and result serialization at line 70: the 200-character query is interpolated twice, enabling predicate/UNION manipulation.

expectations.text: NoSQL injection in review update (operator/$where injection)
expectations.evidence: WSA-008 (report.md:93–97) names routes/updateProductReviews.ts:16 and states 'Non-scalar IDs also reach the database selector' and 'broad operator-based updates'. Source confirms {_id:req.body.id}, $set and multi:true. Supported confidence for unresolved MarsDB behavior is appropriate; operator injection is explicitly identified, not inferred from an ownership finding.

expectations.text: NoSQL injection in order tracking
expectations.evidence: WSA-018 (report.md:167–171) identifies routes/trackOrder.ts:18 interpolating caller ID into quoted $where, permitting disclosure of other orders. Source confirms the string expression and gate-dependent sanitization.

expectations.text: NoSQL $where sleep / injection in review listing
expectations.evidence: WSA-018 names routes/showProductReviews.ts:36 $where concatenation and its busy-wait helper at line 17, with a two-second per-call limit. Source confirms both; no unbounded-loop or MongoDB-server claim is required.

expectations.text: SSTI / code execution via username rendered in pug template
expectations.evidence: WSA-017 (report.md:159–165) traces POST /profile username into '#{...}' detection and direct eval in routes/userProfile.ts:57–65 before Pug compilation. Correct class and sink; challenge gate is explicitly unresolved.

expectations.text: Sandboxed eval of B2B order payload (RCE / DoS)
expectations.evidence: WSA-021 (report.md:189–195) identifies caller-supplied B2B string evaluated in a two-second VM at routes/b2bOrder.ts:23, causing bounded stalls/resource pressure. Source confirms safeEval(orderLinesData) in vm.runInContext. RCE is not needed because the row explicitly includes DoS.

expectations.text: YAML parsing of uploads (yaml bomb)
expectations.evidence: WSA-021 identifies unauthenticated yaml.load followed by JSON.stringify in routes/fileUpload.ts:109–114 and alias graphs multiplying serialization work. Source confirms the exact reconstruction/serialization sink and timeout.

expectations.text: XXE in XML upload (noent)
expectations.evidence: WSA-019 (report.md:175–181) identifies XML uploads, filesystem providers and XML_PARSE_NOENT/DTDLOAD in lib/xml.ts, with expanded content returned through routes/fileUpload.ts. It names XXE/local-file disclosure and bounded entity-expansion risk.

expectations.text: Zip slip in zip upload handling
expectations.evidence: WSA-020 (report.md:183–187) identifies ZIP entry paths resolved beneath uploads/complaints but checked only against the application-root substring, then written via createWriteStream. Source confirms traversal/overwrite path.

expectations.text: Upload size/type enforced client-side or after processing
expectations.evidence: Not identified at the rubric's sink. WSA-027 describes a different unbounded memory-image disk uploader in server.ts; WSA-019/021 describe XML/YAML processing, but never identify fileUpload.ts checkUploadSize/checkFileType as non-enforcing or the advertised client restriction bypass. Source confirms those two checks merely record challenge state then next(); that discovery is not credited because it is absent from the report.

expectations.text: Mass assignment on user registration (role, etc.)
expectations.evidence: WSA-003 (report.md:41–47) traces public /api/Users registration through Finale to models/user.ts role accepting admin/accounting/deluxe with no write allowlist. Source confirms public create hooks, generated resource and role setter/validator.

expectations.text: Weak server-side registration validation (empty email/password, repeat check client-only)
expectations.evidence: WSA-046 (report.md:396–402) identifies registration checks only when email/password/passwordRepeat are all present, then the empty-string password setter hashing without length validation. Source confirms the conditional branch and model setter. The report does not rely solely on UI weakness.

expectations.text: Negative quantity / price manipulation in basket & order
expectations.evidence: WSA-032 (report.md:273–279) names basketItems.ts/models/basketitem.ts missing positive-quantity checks and order.ts stock subtraction, price multiplication and wallet decrement. Source independently confirms checkout arithmetic; impact is bounded to simulated balances.

expectations.text: Deluxe membership payment bypass
expectations.evidence: WSA-033 (report.md:281–287) identifies routes/deluxe.ts allowing unknown/missing paymentMode to skip wallet/card validation and reach role upgrade. Source confirms both branches and unconditional subsequent upgrade.

expectations.text: Coupon codes forgeable (z85, no secret) / expiry not enforced
expectations.evidence: WSA-034 (report.md:289–295) identifies unauthenticated Z85 coupon encoding in lib/insecurity.ts and order.ts legacy campaign expiry depending on client date rather than server time. Source confirms both mechanisms; ordinary monthly coupons do have a current-month check.

expectations.text: Null byte / path filter bypass and directory listing on /ftp
expectations.evidence: WSA-023/024 (report.md:205–219) identify fileServer.ts suffix allowlisting before literal %00 truncation and public /ftp serveIndex. Source confirms checked versus used filename mismatch and public listing.

expectations.text: Access logs served publicly
expectations.evidence: WSA-013/024 identify public /support/logs and combined URL logging, including password-change query values. Source confirms server.ts public mounting and morgan('combined'); no actual live password in logs is asserted.

expectations.text: Admin area guarded only client-side / admin REST without role check
expectations.evidence: WSA-004 (report.md:53–60) identifies Users/authentication-details requiring any JWT rather than admin, enabling ordinary customer enumeration. This satisfies the row's 'admin REST without role check' alternative; source confirms generic authorization middleware without a role gate.

expectations.text: Feedback CRUD without auth or ownership (delete any, forge UserId, zero stars, captcha reuse)
expectations.evidence: WSA-004 identifies public forged UserId feedback creation and any-customer deletion; WSA-036 identifies exposed CAPTCHA answers and replay. Source confirms Feedback item JWT-only policy and CAPTCHA verification without consumption. Zero-star behavior is not explicitly covered, but a substantive class/sink hit is present.

expectations.text: Basket read by ID without ownership check
expectations.evidence: WSA-006 (report.md:73–79) identifies routes/basket.ts:19 selecting basket by requested ID without owner, despite token middleware. The report names the precise owner-check omission.

expectations.text: Basket item add with BasketId from body / duplicate key parsing
expectations.evidence: WSA-007 (report.md:81–87) identifies raw duplicate JSON parsing in routes/basketItems.ts, first BasketId authorization and later BasketId insertion. This directly addresses the row rather than generic basket IDOR.

expectations.text: Product review author taken from body / update without author check
expectations.evidence: WSA-008 identifies public review creation storing request author/message and authenticated update selecting only id with no author predicate. Source independently confirms both handlers and mounts.

expectations.text: Product PUT allowed for non-admin
expectations.evidence: WSA-004 Products row states update authentication is commented out at server.ts:393, allowing anonymous product changes. Source confirms the missing PUT gate and generated Products CRUD.

expectations.text: CSRF on profile update (form POST accepted cross-origin, no token)
expectations.evidence: WSA-031 (report.md:265–271) identifies cookie-authenticated POST /profile via updateUserProfile.ts, URL-encoded bodies and missing CSRF/origin policy. Cookie-delivery/SameSite prerequisites are explicitly bounded.

expectations.text: SSRF via profile image URL fetch
expectations.evidence: WSA-025 (report.md:221–227) identifies routes/profileImageUrlUpload.ts:24 fetch(url) without destination, redirect or network policy and a public response-body file. Source confirms the fetch/persistence flow; no cloud-specific result is invented.

expectations.text: Weak / hard-coded seed credentials and test accounts
expectations.evidence: No weak/hard-coded seed account or frontend test credential is identified. Data initialization coverage explicitly says remaining seed rows are not a full credential audit. WSA-046 weak user-chosen password policy and WSA-011 deterministic OAuth credentials are distinct mechanisms.

expectations.text: Password reset by security question, no rate limit, guessable answers
expectations.evidence: WSA-012 (report.md:119–125) identifies email plus security answer as sufficient reset authority, publicly returned configured answers used by datacreator, and no fresh one-use recovery proof. WSA-037 bounds the actual 100-per-five-minute reset limiter and forwarded-IP weakness rather than falsely asserting no limiter. Source confirms reset, configuration export and seed linkage.

expectations.text: OAuth login derives password from base64(reversed email) client-side
expectations.evidence: WSA-011 (report.md:111–117) identifies frontend OAuth password as Base64(reversed email), then local registration/login; knows-email password recovery is stated with MFA limitation.

expectations.text: Change password skips current-password check when param absent (GET params)
expectations.evidence: WSA-013 identifies query current/new/repeat on a GET and truthy-only current password comparison. Source independently confirms currentPassword && hash(...) and subsequent mutation for cached token identity.

expectations.text: TOTP secret stored in plaintext in users table
expectations.evidence: WSA-010/016/044 identify disclosure of usable TOTP seeds in models, JWTs and whoami, but do not identify plaintext-at-rest storage as a root cause or cite the setup assignment to the ordinary Users string column. Source confirms that storage flaw exists; it is not credited from grader discovery. Strict distinct-mechanism decision; coordinator may judge implicit seed disclosure sufficient.

expectations.text: Weak crypto: MD5 password hashing, hard-coded HMAC/RSA keys
expectations.evidence: WSA-014 identifies unsalted MD5 password hashing and source-fixed HMAC key in lib/insecurity.ts; WSA-002 covers embedded RSA key; WSA-010 covers returned hashes. Source confirms MD5/HMAC and user setter; class and sinks match.

expectations.text: JWT: alg none / RSA public key confusion accepted, legacy express-jwt
expectations.evidence: Not identified as an established vulnerability. 'Legacy dependency hypotheses' explicitly withholds algorithm confusion; JWT section says algorithm-confusion behavior unresolved. WSA-002 key theft and WSA-015/016 lifecycle/purpose flaws are different mechanisms and do not satisfy alg-none/RSA-public-key acceptance.

expectations.text: Hard-coded encryption keys and key files shipped (encryptionkeys/, ctf.key, premium reward AES key)
expectations.evidence: WSA-002 identifies the hard-coded reusable RSA private key in lib/insecurity.ts and its identical public Terraform copy; WSA-024 identifies public /encryptionkeys. Independently normalized key material matches and server public source serving does not redact it. Credit for embedded/shipped secret-key class; premium AES/ctf.key/easter-egg specifics are absent.

expectations.text: Prometheus /metrics unauthenticated
expectations.evidence: Positive controls/unresolved leads, 'Metrics/errors' (report.md:428), explicitly says '/metrics is public' and emits operational/business aggregates, names server.ts:696, and recommends restricting diagnostics. Source confirms unguarded metrics mount and register.metrics(); a numbered High finding is not required.

expectations.text: Verbose error handler / stack traces in responses
expectations.evidence: Same 'Metrics/errors' paragraph identifies always-installed development-style errorhandler at server.ts:702 exposing diagnostic details; WSA-019 also traces parser content into public errors. Source confirms unconditional errorhandler(). No runtime stack capture is required by a source-review rubric.

expectations.text: XSS sinks: search query via bypassSecurityTrustHtml, product description innerHTML, order-id reflection, True-Client-IP stored and rendered, outdated sanitize-html, video subtitle injection into pug, CSP header built from profile image URL
expectations.challenges: localXss, xssBonus, reflectedXss, restfulXss, persistedXssUser, persistedXssFeedback, httpHeaderXss, videoXss, usernameXss
expectations.evidence: WSA-029 (report.md:249–263) traces search q, tracking order ID, product description, admin email and True-Client-IP to explicit Angular trust bypasses and HTML rendering. WSA-020 covers subtitle-to-script extension and unresolved leads cover profile CSP. Multiple correct class/sink pairs satisfy this bundled row; exact sanitizer bypass is correctly not claimed verified.

expectations.text: Open redirect allowlist uses substring match
expectations.evidence: WSA-042 (report.md:363–369) identifies isRedirectAllowed substring acceptance and routes/redirect.ts, with a trusted URL embedded in attacker query as example. Source independently confirms includes(allowedUrl).

expectations.text: JSONP whoami callback leaks email cross-origin
expectations.evidence: WSA-044 (report.md:380–386) identifies cookie-authenticated currentUser.ts JSONP callback exposing user fields cross-origin, with SameSite/cookie prerequisites. Source confirms default email projection, caller field selection and res.jsonp.

expectations.text: Known-vulnerable / typosquatted dependencies pinned in manifests
expectations.challenges: knownVulnerableComponent, typosquattingNpm, typosquattingAngular, supplyChainAttack, csaf, vulnerableDockerImage
expectations.evidence: No established vulnerable/typosquatted dependency is identified. The legacy-dependency paragraph explicitly keeps old manifest versions as unresolved hypotheses and no typosquatted package is named. Conservative calibration is good, but does not satisfy detection.

bonus_expectations.text: Race condition on review likes (routes/likeProductReviews.ts) — timingAttack
bonus_expectations.evidence: WSA-035 identifies likedBy check followed by separate increment, 150 ms delay and later list update. Source independently confirms a non-atomic read/check/write schedule; runtime concurrency remains unexecuted.

bonus_expectations.text: Local file read in data erasure layout param (routes/dataErasure.ts) — lfr
bonus_expectations.evidence: WSA-028 traces caller layout through request-body spread into res.render, weak path substring exclusions and rendered excerpt. Source confirms both gated and fallback body spreads. Correct path/class with Handlebars resolution explicitly conditional.

bonus_expectations.text: Data export matching other users' data (routes/dataExport.ts) — dataExport
bonus_expectations.evidence: WSA-009 identifies lossy vowel-redacted email used for order export authorization and gives colliding synthetic accounts. Source confirms dataExport's identical transform/query and order storage/history linkage.

bonus_expectations.text: Chatbot prompt injection / debug info to non-admins (routes/chat.ts) — chatbotPromptInjection, chatbotGreedyInjection, aiDebugging, systemPromptExtraction
bonus_expectations.evidence: WSA-039 identifies prompt-only coupon eligibility and maximum-discount policy, unbounded z.number tool argument and unconditional coupon generation; client messages, usernames and reviews enter prompt/context. Source confirms the policy/tool mismatch. Debug/prompt extraction specifics are not required for this bundled root-cause credit.

bonus_expectations.text: Web3: reentrancy in wallet contract, NFT mint logic, sandbox route (routes/web3Wallet.ts, routes/nftMint.ts, data/static/web3-snippets) — web3Wallet, nftMint, web3Sandbox
bonus_expectations.evidence: WSA-045's web3Wallet unbounded Set is a distinct availability issue. No reentrancy, NFT mint authorization/logic or sandbox vulnerability is identified; contract correctness is explicitly not reviewed.

bonus_expectations.text: Hidden routes reachable client-side (token sale, score board, privacy policy, IaC files under assets, extra language file, blueprint under public assets) — tokenSale, scoreBoard, misplacedIacFiles, extraLanguage, retrieveBlueprint
bonus_expectations.evidence: WSA-002/024 identify publicly reachable and listed infrastructure Terraform source, including the secret-bearing networking file, with server.ts mount and response path. Source confirms this source-visible IaC exposure. Credit is for the IaC alternative, not inferred detection of hidden token-sale/scoreboard/blueprint routes.
Report mentions continue/restore routes as shared public training state but never identifies forgeable Hashids or lack of authenticity in continue codes.

bonus_expectations.text: SVG/HTML injection into delivery address or similar — svgInjection
bonus_expectations.evidence: No delivery-address or comparable text-field SVG/HTML sink is identified. WSA-026 does establish an alternate active-SVG mechanism, not merely upload acceptance: caller-selected .svg URL bytes are persisted unchanged under the static application origin, allowing active-document navigation when content type/CSP permit. This was source-verified in profileImageUrlUpload.ts and server.ts, but is a different sink/root cause from address-field injection. WSA-030 independently establishes forged-review content reaching document.write. Strict interpretation scores 0; a broad reading of 'or similar' could reasonably credit these genuine alternate SVG/HTML injection paths.

bonus_expectations.text: Missing output encoding of image filename — missingEncoding
bonus_expectations.evidence: No unencoded image-filename rendering issue is identified. Upload path validation and active file publication do not establish the filename-output-encoding root cause.

calibration.assessment: Strong separation of source-level proof, conditional Supported findings, and unresolved leads. No runtime reproduction is claimed. Detailed gates, MFA barriers, cookie/SameSite conditions, Windows specificity, and simulated-payment bounds generally match the available evidence.
caveats: Several Confirmed findings rely on declared Finale/Sequelize semantics rather than installed implementation inspection. This is disclosed globally; source-supported rather than runtime-verified is the correct reading.
Critical eval finding is explicitly gated; High browser/LLM findings remain Supported. These conditional severity labels are not confirmed false positives.
The report's source-line existence validation must not be mistaken for semantic verification.
Conservative withholding of version-only JWT/CVE/sanitizer claims reduces rubric coverage but is not itself an accuracy failure.

false_claims.count_interpretation: No above-Low trap/non-issue was established as false in this adjudication. This is a count of confirmed contradictions found, not proof that all claims are true or a zero false-positive rate.
false_claims.verification_coverage: Entire 606-line report and complete process notes were read. Numerous application control/data paths were independently inspected (see claims and source_verification), but no full transcript, installed dependencies, runtime, browser, LLM or complete external deployment was available. Some report mechanisms and sibling paths were not independently re-traced.
unresolved: Third-party JWT algorithm behavior, sanitization bypasses and native YAML behavior are expressly hypotheses, not scored false positives.
Windows traversal transport behavior, generated ORM semantics and browser/LLM prerequisites remain conditional.
Exact extent of executor source reads and source-only execution cannot be independently verified from process notes.

claims.claim: The public Terraform copy contains the same RSA signing private key as lib/insecurity.ts.
claims.evidence: Independently extracted PEM bodies and normalized literal CR/LF escapes and whitespace: material equal (866 normalized characters each). Read server.ts public /infrastructure source response and lib/terraformCustomization.ts, which renames application strings without removing secrets. No key bytes included in grading.

claims.claim: A customer can transfer an address's ownership through generated PUT and then read it.
claims.evidence: Read server.ts Address PUT: appendUserId only, generated resource by id; lib/insecurity.ts overwrites update body owner; models/address.ts has no owner immutability hook; custom address GET scopes by resulting owner. Finale mutation semantics not executed.

claims.claim: Configuration response leaks recovery answers that authorize password reset.
claims.evidence: Read appConfiguration.ts full config clone minus only llmApiUrl, default.yml recovery-answer fields, datacreator.ts:348–354 consuming those fields, and resetPassword.ts using answer HMAC to authorize reset. Values redacted from grading.

claims.claim: Cached tokens can outlive expiry for cache-only consumers; MFA temporary tokens are not purpose restricted at generic JWT APIs.
claims.evidence: Read tokenMap/get/updateAuthenticatedUsers/appendUserId in lib/insecurity.ts, changePassword.ts cached-token consumption, 2fa.ts type checks and server generic JWT mounts. Direct source policy supports both; installed JWT middleware acceptance and elapsed-time replay were not executed.

claims.claim: Full users can expose sensitive fields through public memories and caller-selectable whoami fields.
claims.evidence: Read memory.ts full User association, models/user.ts lack of default exclusion scope, server public memories mount and currentUser.ts arbitrary field copying. Serialization relies on declared ORM semantics; no live response or populated memory dataset inspected.

claims.claim: Masked-email order authorization collides across users.
claims.evidence: Read order.ts stored vowel replacement, orderHistory.ts and dataExport.ts identical transform for order lookup, and chat.ts identical comparison. Report's synthetic alice/elice pair has the same masked value.

claims.claim: Review attribution can seed attacker HTML into a victim's exported same-origin document.
claims.evidence: Read public createProductReviews body author/message storage, dataExport review selection by victim email and JSON.stringify, frontend data-export document.write. Browser popup/CSP behavior remains unverified, matching report qualification.

claims.claim: Profile URL upload publishes active SVG content under the application origin.
claims.evidence: Read URL-derived extension allowlist containing svg, unchecked fetch bytes persisted to public uploads and static root registration. Content-type/CSP/browser script execution not tested; report labels Supported.

claims.claim: Disk memory upload occurs before authentication without a per-file size bound.
claims.evidence: Read server.ts rest/memories middleware order and uploadToDisk configuration (client MIME mapping, no limits); upload precedes appendUserId. Distinct from core row 11's complaint-upload validation mechanism.

claims.claim: Checkout/payment changes and likes are non-atomic; payment modes and wallet credit fail open.
claims.evidence: Read full order flow, deluxe.ts and wallet.ts; separate inventory read/write and balance read/decrement, unvalidated non-wallet branch, caller balance credit after owned-card lookup; read likes delayed update. No real-money payment integration or concurrency reproduction inferred.

claims.claim: Windows download handlers can traverse using backslashes.
claims.evidence: Read keyServer.ts and fileServer.ts rejecting only '/' before path.resolve and sendFile. Windows path semantics support the conditional concern; did not independently inspect every claimed sibling or execute Express/proxy decoding.

claims.claim: LLM order-tool identity derives from unsigned JWT payload, and coupon policy exists only in prompt.
claims.evidence: Read chat.ts getUserId decode-only, order-tool lookup against that chosen user's email, z.number coupon input and unguarded generateCoupon; server mounts chat publicly. Model tool selection not verified; report explicitly conditions end-to-end result.

claims.claim: Anonymous chat lacks local request/user/provider-spend budgets.
claims.evidence: Read public chat mount and streamText options: client history, ten-step limit, no output-token budget or handler quota/disconnect cancellation. Provider quota/cost impact depends on external configuration; no provider call made.

claims.claim: Chat history persists after logout and is shared across accounts on one browser profile.
claims.evidence: Read single-key conversation-storage service, navbar/sidenav logout bodies and welcome-screen getAll. Logout removes authentication/basket state but never the shared conversation key.

claims.claim: Anonymous addresses, CAPTCHAs and MIME metric labels can accumulate without bounded lifecycle.
claims.evidence: Read web3Wallet Set insertion before provider setup with only matching event deletion, captcha insert/non-consuming verify, server public mounts and metrics file.mimetype labels. No exhaustion threshold or dependency memory measurement verified.

claims.claim: Supplied Terraform HTTP listener forwards application traffic without redirect.
claims.evidence: Read terraform/networking.tf HTTP default_action forward and separate HTTPS listener. Actual deployment/edge policy not verified, as report states.

claims.claim: All 61 routes, 23 models, 214 complete source paths were read and no app/network/test execution occurred.
claims.evidence: process.md contains an extensive read ledger and source-only tool description, but no full execution transcript is available. Inventory metadata cannot prove full semantic reads or absence of other actions.

claims.claim: All 201 explicit source references resolve and every finding includes fix/regression guidance.
claims.evidence: Report read fully and finding structure inspected; substantive source checks were extensive but this grader did not re-run every path/line existence check. Existence alone would not establish semantic correctness.

inventory.credit_policy: Inventory matches do not receive finding or read-coverage credit by themselves.

source_verification.method: Read-only static source inspection; no target execution, dependency install, live testing or external browsing.
special_checks: Normalized RSA private-key material equality between lib/insecurity.ts and infrastructure/terraform/networking.tf was true; no key bytes included in grading.
source_verification.limits: The listed reads are semantic spot/adjudication checks, not an independent complete re-audit or exhaustive verification of all 46 findings. Correct report anchors without independent flow checks are not labeled source-verified here.

rubric_omissions.note: These are detection omissions, not false claims.

ambiguities_for_coordinator.reason: Report proves TOTP-secret exposure but never explicitly identifies plaintext database storage. Strict separate-mechanism interpretation; a broader implicit-storage reading would produce 36/40.

Credit for explicitly hard-coded shipped RSA secret in a named rubric anchor; premium/easter-egg AES and ctf.key mechanisms are not described. Bundled row does not state all listed subcases are mandatory.
Credit for concrete public IaC exposure, one listed alternative; source copy uses /infrastructure rather than assets. Hidden client route enumeration is absent.

Report establishes genuine alternate SVG/HTML injection: WSA-026 traces unvalidated SVG bytes to same-origin static publication plus active-document navigation prerequisites; WSA-030 traces review text to document.write. They are not mere upload acceptance. Scored 0 under a strict delivery-address/text-field root-cause interpretation; broad 'or similar' interpretation could score 1.
Explicit class and sink appear in bounded observations, not numbered findings; rubric says report must name class/sink, not severity or numbered-finding status.

uncertainties: No user_notes.md exists; process.md documents missing runtime/gate/library/edge evidence and unmeasured audit-wide timing/tokens.
needs_review: Coordinator adjudication of the listed row-boundary interpretations.
workarounds: Self-reported truncated source batches were reread; inventory excerpts were redacted; speculative tracking path traversal was withdrawn after encodeURIComponent check.

execution_metrics.reason: No executor metrics.json or full transcript supplied. Output byte counts are not token telemetry.

timing.reason: No timing.json supplied; process explicitly reports no measured audit-wide elapsed/token count.

suggestions.reason: Specify whether reporting usable TOTP seed exposure counts as plaintext-at-rest detection; current wording separates these classes but leaves implicit recognition ambiguous.

Bundled independent mechanisms and 'or similar' allow inconsistent any-versus-all coverage. Define per-row minimum class/sink evidence, especially for active SVG upload versus address injection and public IaC versus hidden UI routes.

The frozen row says 'no rate limit', while supplied server.ts has a 100/5-minute reset limit. Grade the actual weak recovery and limiter-bypass mechanisms without rewarding a contradicted absolute statement.

eval_feedback.overall: Rubric provides useful root-cause coverage but is not comprehensive: several substantiated new identity, serialization, storage and LLM findings remain outside the 40-row score. Keep those qualitative findings separate rather than adding ad hoc core points.
